newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka to sign telecom deal with NTT.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka to sign telecom deal with NTT.

text.p: Sri Lanka will sign an agreement on Tuesday to sell a 35 percent equity stake in the state-owned telephone monopoly Sri Lanka Telecom to Japan's Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT), a senior government official said.

"The signing will take place at 11 a.m. local time (0500 GMT) to sell 35 percent of Sri Lanka Telecom to NTT for $225 million," Mano Tittawella, director-general of the Public Enterprise Reform Commission (PERC), told Reuters.

Under the terms of the strategic partnership which will be formed between the Sri Lanka government and NTT, the Japanese firm will appoint a chief executive officer and several senior executives to take care of the joint venture, said a joint statement from NTT and the government.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and Development Finance Corporation Ltd were financial advisers on the restructuring, Tittawella said.
PERC, which oversees privatisations and restructuring of loss-making public enterprises, began working on the Sri Lanka telecom deal in April 1996.
